claim: Phosphotyrosine (pTyr) motifs in unstructured polypeptides orchestrate important cellular processes by engaging SH2-containing adaptors to assemble complex signalling networks.
source: Phosphotyrosine (pTyr) motifs in unstructured polypeptides orchestrate important cellular processes by engaging SH2-containing adaptors to assemble complex signalling networks.
evidence: This is a general statement about pTyr motifs supported by established scientific knowledge in the field.

claim: The signalling cascade driving actin-based motility and spread of Vaccinia virus involves two pTyr motifs in the viral protein A36 that recruit the adaptors Nck and Grb2.
source: This network involves two pTyr motifs in the viral protein A36 that recruit the adaptors Nck and Grb2 upstream of N-WASP and Arp2/3 complex-mediated actin polymerisation.
evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript and citations to prior work.

claim: Only specific spatial arrangements of Nck and Grb2 binding sites result in robust N-WASP recruitment, Arp2/3 complex driven actin polymerisation and viral spread.
source: Manipulating the position of pTyr motifs in A36 and the unrelated p14 from Orthoreovirus, we find that only specific spatial arrangements of Nck and Grb2 binding sites result in robust N-WASP recruitment, Arp2/3 complex driven actin polymerisation and viral spread.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from manipulating pTyr motif positions in A36 and p14.

claim: The relative position of pTyr adaptor binding sites is optimised for signal output.
source: This suggests that the relative position of pTyr adaptor binding sites is optimised for signal output.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental observations about spatial arrangements.

claim: The relative positions of pTyr motifs are frequently conserved in proteins from widely different species.
source: This finding may explain why the relative positions of pTyr motifs are frequently conserved in proteins from widely different species.
evidence: This is supported by sequence alignment data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B and general knowledge.

claim: pTyr signals are extensively used by multicellular animals for growth, communication, movement, and differentiation.
source: Multicellular animals extensively use phosphotyrosine (pTyr) signals for growth, communication, movement, and differentiation (Jin and Pawson, 2012; Lim and Pawson, 2010).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Pathways including EGF and insulin receptor signalling, as well as T cell activation rely on pTyr motifs interacting with SH2 domains.
source: Pathways including EGF and insulin receptor signalling, as well as T cell activation rely on pTyr motifs interacting with SH2 domains (Blumenthal and Burkhardt, 2020; Lemmon and Schlessinger, 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: SH2 domains are present in kinases, phosphatases as well as adaptor proteins that lack enzymatic activity but couple upstream signalling events to downstream function.
source: SH2 domains are present in kinases, phosphatases as well as adaptor proteins that lack enzymatic activity but couple upstream signalling events to downstream function (Liu and Nash, 2012).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: pTyr signalling is often dysregulated in cancers and other diseases.
source: pTyr signalling is often dysregulated in cancers and other diseases.
evidence: This is supported by general knowledge and citations in the following sentence.

claim: EGF receptors can be mutationally activated or present in high copy numbers vis-à-vis their cognate adaptors.
source: For example, EGF receptors can be mutationally activated or present in high copy numbers vis-à-vis their cognate adaptors, and oncogenic mutations frequently map to SH2 domains (Li et al., 2012a; Li et al., 2021; Shi et al., 2016; Sigismund et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Oncogenic mutations frequently map to SH2 domains.
source: For example, EGF receptors can be mutationally activated or present in high copy numbers vis-à-vis their cognate adaptors, and oncogenic mutations frequently map to SH2 domains (Li et al., 2012a; Li et al., 2021; Shi et al., 2016; Sigismund et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: pTyr motifs commonly occur in poorly ordered, unstructured regions of proteins.
source: pTyr motifs commonly occur in poorly ordered, unstructured regions of proteins (Stavropoulos et al., 2012; Van Roey et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: The C terminus of EGFR is disordered.
source: Indeed, like many receptor tyrosine kinases, the C terminus of EGFR is disordered (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A; Keppel et al., 2017; Pinet et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by citations and data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The C-terminal region of EGFR contains several pTyr motifs including those that bind Grb2 and Shc1.
source: This region contains several pTyr motifs including those that bind Grb2 and Shc1 (Batzer et al., 1994; Lin et al., 2019; Mandiyan et al., 1996; Smith et al., 2006; Ward et al., 1996).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: The relative positions of Grb2 and Shc1 binding motifs in EGFR are conserved across vertebrates.
source: The relative positions of these motifs are conserved across vertebrates (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is supported by sequence alignment data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Disordered sequences can become structured when bound to their respective domains.
source: Additionally, disordered sequences can become structured when bound to their respective domains (Davey, 2019; Nioche et al., 2002; van der Lee et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Integral membrane proteins with disordered cytoplasmic regions involved in multivalent pTyr-SH2 interactions such as LAT and nephrin form phase separated condensates at critical concentrations.
source: Integral membrane proteins with disordered cytoplasmic regions and involved in multivalent pTyr-SH2 interactions such as Linker for Activation of T cells (LAT) and the kidney podocyte regulator nephrin form phase separated condensates at critical concentrations (Case et al., 2019; Ditlev et al., 2019; Kim et al., 2019; Pak et al., 2016; Su et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: The property of forming phase separated condensates is thought to contribute to the signalling function of LAT and nephrin.
source: This striking property is thought to contribute to their signalling function.
evidence: This is a speculative statement based on inference from prior observations.

claim: Following replication and assembly, Vaccinia virus recruits kinesin-1 via WD/WE motifs in the cytoplasmic tail of A36 to transport virions to the cell periphery on microtubules.
source: Following replication and assembly, Vaccinia virus recruits kinesin-1 via WD/WE motifs in the cytoplasmic tail of A36 an integral viral membrane protein to transport virions to the cell periphery on microtubules (Dodding et al., 2011; Figure 1).
evidence: This is supported by a citation and illustrated in Figure 1.

claim: After viral fusion with the plasma membrane, extracellular virions that remain attached to the cell locally activate Src and Abl family kinases.
source: After viral fusion with the plasma membrane, extracellular virions that remain attached to the cell locally activate Src and Abl family kinases (Frischknecht et al., 1999; Newsome et al., 2004; Newsome et al., 2006; Reeves et al., 2005).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Src and Abl family kinases phosphorylate tyrosine 112 and 132 in a disordered region of A36 once it incorporates into the plasma membrane.
source: This results in phosphorylation of tyrosine 112 and 132 in a disordered region of A36 once it incorporates into the plasma membrane when the virus fuses at the cell periphery (Frischknecht et al., 1999; Newsome et al., 2004; Newsome et al., 2006; Reeves et al., 2005; Ward and Moss, 2004; Figure 1, Figure 1—figure supplement 1 – supplement 1C).
evidence: This is supported by citations and illustrated in figures.

claim: pTyr 112 and 132 motifs in A36 bind the SH2 domains of adaptors Nck and Grb2, respectively.
source: pTyr 112 and 132 motifs bind the SH2 domains of adaptors Nck and Grb2, respectively (Scaplehorn et al., 2002).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: Nck recruits N-WASP via WIP to activate the Arp2/3 complex at the virus.
source: Nck recruits N-WASP via WIP to activate the Arp2/3 complex at the virus (Donnelly et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: Arp2/3 complex-mediated actin polymerisation drives virus motility and enhances its cell-to-cell spread.
source: The resulting actin polymerisation drives virus motility and enhances its cell-to-cell spread (Ward and Moss, 2004).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: Nck is essential for actin tail formation in Vaccinia virus.
source: Nck is essential for actin tail formation, while Grb2 recruitment helps stabilise the signalling complex (Frischknecht et al., 1999; Scaplehorn et al., 2002; Weisswange et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Grb2 recruitment helps stabilise the Vaccinia virus signalling complex.
source: Nck is essential for actin tail formation, while Grb2 recruitment helps stabilise the signalling complex (Frischknecht et al., 1999; Scaplehorn et al., 2002; Weisswange et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: NPF motifs in A36 interact with the RhoGEF intersectin to recruit Cdc42 and clathrin to the virus, further enhancing actin polymerisation.
source: Additionally, NPF motifs in A36 interact with the RhoGEF intersectin to recruit Cdc42 and clathrin to the virus, further enhancing actin polymerisation (Humphries et al., 2012; Humphries et al., 2014; Snetkov et al., 2016; Figure 1).
evidence: This is supported by citations and illustrated in Figure 1.

claim: The turnover rates of Nck, Grb2, and N-WASP beneath extracellular virions are highly reproducible with little variability.
source: The turnover rates of Nck, Grb2, and N-WASP beneath extracellular virions are highly reproducible with little variability, suggesting the signalling network has a defined organisation (Weisswange et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: The Vaccinia virus signalling network has a defined organisation.
source: The turnover rates of Nck, Grb2, and N-WASP beneath extracellular virions are highly reproducible with little variability, suggesting the signalling network has a defined organisation (Weisswange et al., 2009).
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the reproducibility of turnover rates.

claim: Both WIP and N-WASP only have two Nck-binding sites, each with distinct preferences for the three adaptor SH3 domains.
source: This underlying organisation may arise from the fact that both WIP and N-WASP only have two Nck-binding sites, each with distinct preferences for the three adaptor SH3 domains (Donnelly et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: The Nck-dependent signalling network is used by nephrin in kidney podocytes and the pathogenic E. coli EPEC protein Tir to polymerise actin.
source: This Nck-dependent signalling network is not unique to Vaccinia and is also used to polymerise actin by nephrin in kidney podocytes and the pathogenic E. coli EPEC protein Tir (Hayward et al., 2006; Jones et al., 2006; Welch and Way, 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: A recombinant virus expressing A36 that terminates after the Grb2 binding site at residue 139 (A36 N-G virus) retains the WD/WE kinesin-1 binding motifs required for microtubule-based transport.
source: To achieve this goal, the WR–ΔA36R virus lacking the A36 gene was rescued with an A36 variant that terminates after the Grb2 binding site at residue 139 (referred to as the A36 N-G virus hereafter). This shorter A36 variant retains the WD/WE kinesin-1 binding motifs that are required for microtubule-based transport of the virus to the plasma membrane.
evidence: This is a description of the experimental construct design.

claim: Actin tail formation induced by the truncated A36 variant depends on the Nck-binding site.
source: As in the full-length protein, actin tail formation induced by this shorter A36 variant depends on the Nck-binding site (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A, A36 N-G vs X-G).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Truncated A36 induces shorter actin tails in the absence of Grb2 recruitment.
source: Similar to the intact protein, truncated A36 induces shorter actin tails in the absence of Grb2 recruitment (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A, A36 N-G vs N-X).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Exchanging the positions of Nck and Grb2 binding motifs in A36 impacts the length of actin tails.
source: Strikingly, exchanging the positions of these two pTyr motifs impacts the length of actin tails though the number of extracellular virus particles inducing actin polymerisation remains unaltered (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: The number of extracellular virus particles inducing actin polymerisation remains unaltered when the positions of Nck and Grb2 binding motifs are exchanged.
source: Strikingly, exchanging the positions of these two pTyr motifs impacts the length of actin tails though the number of extracellular virus particles inducing actin polymerisation remains unaltered (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Viruses A36 N-X and X-N that lack a Grb2 binding site did not differ considerably in their extent or ability to induce actin tails.
source: We found that viruses A36 N-X and X-N that lack a Grb2 binding site (N-X: Nck binds in native position and X-N: Nck binds in Grb2 position), did not differ considerably in their extent or ability to induce actin tails, although there is a mild impact on actin tail length (p=0.18) (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Having two Nck or Grb2 binding sites does not improve the ability of a single adaptor to promote actin polymerisation.
source: Curiously, having two Nck or Grb2 binding sites does not improve the ability of a single adaptor to promote actin polymerisation (Figure 2—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2A.

claim: The length of actin tails was not influenced by extending the linker between the adaptor binding sites.
source: The length of actin tails was also not influenced by extending the linker between the adaptor binding sites (Figure 2—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2B.

claim: The relative positioning and number of Nck and Grb2 phosphotyrosine motifs in A36 is optimised for efficient actin polymerisation.
source: Collectively, our observations suggest that the relative positioning and number of Nck and Grb2 phosphotyrosine motifs in A36 is optimised for the signalling output (efficient actin polymerisation).
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental observations.

claim: In the swapped configuration (A36 G-N), virus motility is slower compared to A36 N-G.
source: In the swapped configuration, corresponding to reduced actin polymerisation, virus motility is slower (Figure 2C, Video 1).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2C and Video 1.

claim: The A36 G-N virus has reduced cell-to-cell spread as it forms smaller plaques on confluent cell monolayers compared to A36 N-G.
source: In addition, the A36 G-N virus has reduced cell-to-cell spread as it forms smaller plaques on confluent cell monolayers compared to A36 N-G (Figure 2D; Figure 2—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2D and Figure 2—figure supplement 1C.

claim: The output of a signalling network is strongly influenced by the relative positioning of Nck and Grb2 binding sites in the membrane protein responsible for initiating the signalling cascade.
source: Our observations with Vaccinia clearly demonstrate that the output of a signalling network is strongly influenced by the relative positioning of Nck and Grb2 binding sites in the membrane protein responsible for initiating the signalling cascade.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental observations with Vaccinia.

claim: p14, an integral membrane protein from Orthoreovirus, activates N-WASP via Grb2 to regulate cell fusion.
source: Recent observations, however, demonstrate that p14, an integral membrane protein from Orthoreovirus activates N-WASP via Grb2 to regulate cell fusion (Chan et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: Grb2 is recruited by a pTyr116 motif located in the short cytoplasmic tail of p14.
source: Grb2 is recruited by a pTyr116 motif located in the short cytoplasmic tail of p14 that is also predicted to be disordered (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is supported by a citation and disorder prediction shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1C.

claim: There are two tyrosine residues in p14 predicted to interact with Nck located 16 and 20 amino acids upstream of the pTyr116.
source: Interestingly, examination of the p14 sequence reveals there are two tyrosine residues predicted to interact with Nck located 16 and 20 amino acids upstream of the pTyr116 (Eukaryotic Linear Motif (ELM) and Scansite 4.0) (Kumar et al., 2020; Obenauer et al., 2003; Figure 3A).
evidence: This is based on bioinformatic predictions using ELM and Scansite tools.

claim: Transient expression of p14 N-G in cells infected with Vaccinia virus lacking A36 results in extracellular virions inducing robust actin tails that were dependent on the presence of N-WASP.
source: Transient expression of p14 N-G in cells infected with Vaccinia virus lacking A36 results in extracellular virions inducing robust actin tails that were dependent on the presence of N-WASP (Figure 3B and C).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3B and C.

claim: Tyr96 in p14 is essential for virus induced actin polymerisation.
source: In contrast, Tyr96 is essential for the virus induced actin polymerisation.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from mutational analysis.

claim: There is no role for Tyr100 in p14 actin tail formation.
source: This analysis reveals there is no role for Tyr100 as its mutation to phenylalanine had no impact on actin tail formation (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: The ability of transiently expressed p14 N-G to promote actin polymerisation primarily depends on the predicted Nck-binding pTyr96 and is enhanced by pTyr116.
source: As with Vaccinia A36, the ability of transiently expressed p14 N-G to promote actin polymerisation primarily depends on the predicted Nck-binding pTyr96 and is enhanced by pTyr116 (Figure 3D and E).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3D and E.

claim: Disrupting pTyr96 and pTyr116 sites in p14 N-G results in loss of Nck and Grb2 recruitment to the virus respectively.
source: Disrupting these sites via Y96F and Y116F mutations in p14 N-G results in loss of Nck and Grb2 recruitment to the virus respectively (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A.

claim: When phosphorylated, Tyr116 in p14 is a bona fide Grb2-binding site.
source: When phosphorylated, Tyr116 is a bona fide Grb2-binding site (Chan et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: The pTyr96 peptide from p14 retains Nck from cell lysate but not the unphosphorylated control.
source: The pTyr96 peptide retains Nck from the cell lysate but not the unphosphorylated control (Figure 3F).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3F.

claim: The pTyr96 peptide from p14 does not bind Grb2.
source: The peptide also does not bind Grb2.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from peptide pulldown assays.

claim: The pTyr100 peptide from p14 does not bind either Nck or Grb2.
source: Consistent with our observation that Tyr100 plays no part in actin polymerisation, the pTyr100 peptide does not bind either adaptor (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1B.

claim: p14 of Orthoreovirus induces actin polymerisation using a Nck and Grb2 signalling network.
source: Our observations clearly demonstrate that as with Vaccinia A36, p14 of Orthoreovirus induces actin polymerisation using a Nck and Grb2 signalling network.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental observations with p14.

claim: The Vaccinia platform can be used to establish synthetic signalling networks and test predictions concerning their operation.
source: These results also establish that the Vaccinia platform can be used to establish synthetic signalling networks and test predictions concerning their operation.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the successful use of the p14 construct in the Vaccinia system.

claim: Actin tails generated by the p14 N-G virus recruit endogenous Nck, WIP, and N-WASP to the virion.
source: As previously observed with Vaccinia A36, actin tails generated by the p14 N-G virus recruit endogenous Nck, WIP, and N-WASP to the virion (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: The p14 N-G virus recruits Grb2.
source: We next sought to determine whether the relative positioning of the Nck and Grb2 binding sites was important for the signalling output of p14. To address this question, we generated a recombinant virus (p14 G-N virus) where the Nck- and Grb2-binding motifs of p14 are in a swapped orientation (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is implied by the experimental design and confirmed in Figure 4A.

claim: Swapping the Nck and Grb2 binding motifs in p14 did not impact on the number of viruses inducing actin polymerisation but resulted in shorter actin tails and a slower virus speed.
source: Remarkably, as we observed for A36, swapping these motifs did not impact on the number of viruses inducing actin polymerisation but resulted in shorter actin tails and a slower virus speed (Figure 4C and D, Video 2).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4C and D, and Video 2.

claim: The p14 G-N virus is attenuated in its spread when compared to p14 N-G.
source: Plaque assays on confluent cell monolayers reveals that the p14 G-N virus is also attenuated in its spread when compared to p14 N-G (Figure 4E).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4E.

claim: The signalling output of the p14 system depends on the relative positioning of Nck and Grb2 pTyr binding sites.
source: Once again, the signalling output of the system clearly depends on the relative positioning of Nck and Grb2 pTyr binding sites.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental observations with p14.

claim: There is no significant difference between the levels of A36 N-G and G-N relative to RFP-A3 on particles generating actin tails.
source: We found no significant difference between the levels of A36 N-G and G-N relative to RFP-A3 on particles generating actin tails (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The levels of Nck are comparable between the A36 N-G and G-N viruses.
source: We found that the levels of Nck are comparable between the A36 N-G and G-N viruses (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: Grb2 and N-WASP were significantly reduced on the A36 G-N virus compared to A36 N-G.
source: In contrast, Grb2 and N-WASP were significantly reduced on the G-N virus (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: The level of WIP is lower in the A36 G-N configuration compared to A36 N-G.
source: The level of WIP, which is also recruited to actin tails is lower in the G-N configuration (Figure 5—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1C.

claim: The A36 G-N virus recruited twofold less GFP-N-WASP than the N-G variant in MEF cells.
source: We found that as seen in HeLa cells, the levels of GFP-Nck were similar for both viruses but the A36 G-N virus recruited twofold less GFP-N-WASP than the N-G variant (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Loss of Grb2 binding had no appreciable impact on the levels of Nck recruited to the A36 N-X virus.
source: Loss of Grb2 binding had no appreciable impact on the levels of Nck recruited to the A36 N-X virus as compared to those associated with the A36 N-G and G-N viruses (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: The levels of N-WASP on the A36 N-X virus were reduced (46.4%) but not to the same extent as the A36 G-N virus (75%).
source: The levels of N-WASP on the A36 N-X virus were reduced (46.4%) but not to the same extent as the A36 G-N virus (75%).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data comparing N-WASP levels.

claim: Repositioning the Nck and Grb2 sites leads to a more severe impairment of the ability of the signalling network to activate Arp2/3 complex driven actin polymerisation than loss of the Grb2 site.
source: Repositioning the Nck and Grb2 sites clearly leads to a more severe impairment of the ability of the signalling network to activate Arp2/3 complex driven actin polymerisation than loss of the Grb2 site.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from comparing the effects of motif swapping versus Grb2 site loss.

claim: Grb2 has a dominant negative effect when it is mis-positioned relative to Nck.
source: Moreover, this suggests that Grb2 has a dominant negative effect when it is mis-positioned relative to Nck.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the observation that motif swapping is worse than Grb2 site loss.

claim: A36 phosphorylation in the A36 G-N virus infected cells is comparable to that seen with the A36 N-G virus.
source: Immunoblot analysis of whole cell lysates with anti-phosphotyrosine antibody demonstrates that A36 phosphorylation in the A36 G-N virus infected cells is comparable to that seen with the A36 N-G virus (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The A36 N-G and G-N viruses recruit similar levels of Src kinase.
source: Quantification of Src-GFP at the tip of actin tails reveals that the A36 N-G and G-N viruses recruit similar levels of the tyrosine kinase (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: A similar level of activated Src kinase (Src pY418) is associated with both A36 N-G and G-N viruses.
source: Furthermore, immunofluorescence analysis with a Src antibody that detects phosphorylated tyrosine 418 (Src pY418) reveals a similar level of activated kinase is associated with both viruses (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: Both A36 N-G and G-N viruses were equally efficient at recruiting GFP-Nck SH2.
source: We found that both A36 N-G and G-N viruses were equally efficient at recruiting GFP-Nck SH2 (Figure 6C).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6C.

claim: Phosphorylation of the Nck binding motif (Tyr112) is not affected by its position in A36.
source: These data clearly demonstrate that phosphorylation of the Nck binding motif is not affected by its position.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the GFP-Nck SH2 recruitment data.

claim: Tyrosine 132 is phosphorylated on the A36 N-G and G-N but not N-X virus particles inducing actin tails.
source: Immunofluorescence analysis with an antibody that detects pTyr132 (Newsome et al., 2004) reveals that tyrosine 132 is phosphorylated on the A36 N-G and G-N but not N-X (negative control lacking Grb2 binding site) virus particles inducing actin tails (Figure 6D).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6D.

claim: The intensity of pTyr132 antibody labelling was significantly higher on the A36 G-N compared to the N-G virus.
source: Moreover, the intensity of labelling was significantly higher on the G-N compared to the N-G virus, suggesting there is no impairment in phosphorylation.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from antibody labelling.

claim: The enhanced pTyr132 antibody labelling intensity on A36 G-N most likely reflects increased antibody access to its epitope in the absence of Grb2 recruitment.
source: This enhanced labelling intensity most likely reflects increased antibody access to its pTyr132 epitope in the absence of Grb2 recruitment (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the observation of higher antibody signal when Grb2 is reduced.

claim: There was a trend for increased pTyr132 antibody labelling on the A36 N-G virus when the levels of Grb2 were reduced by siRNA knockdown.
source: We found that there was a trend for increased labelling on the A36 N-G virus when the levels of Grb2 were reduced (Figure 6—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1C.

claim: The lower levels of Grb2 recruitment observed when its binding site is repositioned are a consequence of other changes in the signalling network rather than a reduction in phosphorylation of Tyr132.
source: Taken together, our observations suggest that the lower levels of Grb2 recruitment observed when its binding site is repositioned are a consequence of other changes in the signalling network rather than a reduction in phosphorylation of Tyr132.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the phosphorylation and recruitment data.

claim: All four viruses (A36 N-G, G-N, G-N-G, and G-G-N) recruited similar levels of Nck and induced comparable numbers of actin tails.
source: All four viruses (N-G, G-N, G-N-G, and G-G-N) recruited similar levels of Nck and induced comparable numbers of actin tails (Figure 7—figure supplement 1A and B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1A and B.

claim: The A36 G-N and G-G-N viruses induced equally short actin tails.
source: Nevertheless, the A36 G-N and G-G-N viruses induced the formation of equally short actin tails (Figure 7B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7B.

claim: The actin tails formed by the A36 G-N-G virus are noticeably longer than those formed by A36 G-N.
source: In contrast, the actin tails formed by the A36 G-N-G virus are noticeably longer.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data comparing actin tail lengths.

claim: A similar trend for virus speed and spread was observed for the A36 G-N-G virus compared to G-N and G-G-N.
source: A similar trend was also observed for virus speed and spread (Figure 7C and D; Figure 7—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7C and D, and Figure 7—figure supplement 2.

claim: The A36 G-N-G and N-G viruses recruit similar levels of N-WASP, which are ~2 fold greater than the G-G-N and G-N viruses.
source: Strikingly, the G-N-G and N-G viruses recruit similar levels of N-WASP, which are ~2 fold greater than the G-G-N and G-N viruses (Figure 7E).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7E.

claim: The A36 G-N-G and N-G viruses recruit significantly more GFP-Grb2 than G-G-N and G-N viruses.
source: They also recruit significantly more GFP-Grb2 (Figure 7—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1C.

claim: The binding position of Grb2 relative to Nck influences the level of N-WASP recruitment.
source: Grb2 is not essential for Vaccinia actin tail formation but its binding position relative to Nck clearly influences the level of N-WASP recruitment.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental observations with multiple Grb2 sites.

claim: The binding position of Grb2 relative to Nck influences the output of the signalling network stimulated by phosphorylation of A36.
source: This subsequently influences the output of the signalling network stimulated by phosphorylation of A36.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental observations.

claim: Nck and Grb2 are multivalent adaptors that interact with N-WASP to activate the Arp2/3 complex.
source: Nck and Grb2 are multivalent adaptors that interact with N-WASP to activate the Arp2/3 complex.
evidence: This is supported by established knowledge in the field.

claim: Grb2 has two SH3 domains that bind N-WASP.
source: Grb2 has two SH3 domains that bind N-WASP while the three SH3 domains of Nck engage with WIP and N-WASP (Carlier et al., 2000; Donnelly et al., 2013; Rivera et al., 2004).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: The three SH3 domains of Nck engage with WIP and N-WASP.
source: Grb2 has two SH3 domains that bind N-WASP while the three SH3 domains of Nck engage with WIP and N-WASP (Carlier et al., 2000; Donnelly et al., 2013; Rivera et al., 2004).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: The linker between the first and second Nck SH3 domains contributes to N-WASP activation.
source: The linker between the first and second Nck SH3 domains also contributes to N-WASP activation (Banjade et al., 2015; Bywaters and Rivera, 2021; Okrut et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: There are 11 predicted class I SH3-binding PxxP motifs in human N-WASP.
source: Bioinformatic analysis (scan site and ELM) reveals there are 11 and 17 predicted class I and class II SH3-binding PxxP motifs in human N-WASP and WIP, respectively.
evidence: This is based on bioinformatic predictions.

claim: There are 17 predicted class II SH3-binding PxxP motifs in human WIP.
source: Bioinformatic analysis (scan site and ELM) reveals there are 11 and 17 predicted class I and class II SH3-binding PxxP motifs in human N-WASP and WIP, respectively.
evidence: This is based on bioinformatic predictions.

claim: Grb2-binding pTyr motifs N-terminal to that of Nck lead to reduced recruitment of Grb2 and N-WASP.
source: We find that Grb2-binding pTyr motifs N-terminal to that of Nck lead to reduced recruitment of Grb2 and N-WASP.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from the motif swapping experiments.

claim: There are preferred configurations of SH3-PxxP interactions to achieve optimal signalling output (actin polymerisation) via Nck/Grb2/N-WASP.
source: This suggests that there are preferred configurations of SH3-PxxP interactions to achieve optimal signalling output (actin polymerisation) via Nck/Grb2/N-WASP.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental observations.

claim: WIP and N-WASP each only contain two Nck-binding PxxP sites with differing preferences for the individual SH3 domains of Nck.
source: Consistent with this, our previous far western analysis demonstrates that WIP and N-WASP each only contain two Nck-binding PxxP sites (Donnelly et al., 2013). Moreover, these sites have differing preferences for the individual SH3 domains of Nck.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior work from the authors' lab.

claim: Some cellular condensates such as P granules, stress granules, and puncta formed by FUS have underlying organisational principles.
source: Recent evidence also indicates that the function of some cellular condensates such as P granules, stress granules, and puncta formed by FUS (fused in sarcoma) have underlying organisational principles (Bienz, 2020; Folkmann et al., 2021; Jain et al., 2016; Kato and McKnight, 2017; Kato et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: There is a degree of defined, spatial organisation within the interactions in membrane-associated signalling networks.
source: It may be, as our observations suggest, there is a degree of defined, spatial organisation within the interactions in membrane-associated signalling networks.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental observations.

claim: Src/Abl family kinases are constitutively associated with Vaccinia viruses undergoing actin-dependent motility.
source: Unlike many systems where kinases transiently associate with their substrates, Src/Abl family kinases are constitutively associated with Vaccinia viruses undergoing actin-dependent motility.
evidence: This is supported by prior knowledge about the Vaccinia system.

claim: Repositioning of A36 tyrosine motifs did not impact the levels of total or activated Src kinase detected at the virus.
source: Importantly, repositioning of A36 tyrosine motifs did not impact the levels of total or activated Src kinase detected at the virus (Figure 6A and B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6A and B.

claim: Swapping Nck and Grb2-binding motifs in A36 does not detectably impair their phosphorylation.
source: However, swapping Nck and Grb2-binding motifs in A36 does not detectably impair their phosphorylation (Figure 6C and D, Figure 6—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6C and D, and Figure 6—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The ~20 amino acid spacing between SH2-binding sites in Vaccinia A36 and Orthoreovirus p14 is also observed in LAT, nephrin, and EGFR.
source: It is striking that the ~20 amino acid spacing between SH2-binding sites in Vaccinia A36 and Orthoreovirus p14 is also observed in the Grb2-binding Tyr171 and Tyr191 in LAT (Huang et al., 2017), Nck-binding Tyr1176, Tyr1193, Tyr1217 in nephrin (Jones et al., 2006) and Grb2-binding Tyr1092 and Tyr1110 in EGFR (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is supported by citations and data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The Nck1 SH2 domain has a footprint of 12 residues when bound to a phosphopeptide of Tir.
source: The Nck1 SH2 domain has a footprint of 12 residues when bound to a phosphopeptide (EEHI-pY-DEVAADP) of Tir (PDB 2CI9), which is responsible for inducing EPEC actin pedestals (Frese et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to structural data.

claim: Structures of Grb2-bound phosphopeptides indicate that the adaptor has an even smaller footprint than that of Nck.
source: Furthermore, structures of Grb2-bound phosphopeptides (PDB 1TZE, PDB 1JYR) indicate that the adaptor has an even smaller footprint than that of Nck (Rahuel et al., 1996; Nioche et al., 2002).
evidence: This is supported by citations to structural data.

claim: The SH2 domain of Grb2 is unique because its cognate pTyr motif adopts a β-turn conformation when bound rather than an extended conformation.
source: An additional consideration is that the SH2 domain of Grb2 is unique compared to others because its cognate pTyr motif adopts a β-turn conformation when bound rather than an extended conformation (Ettmayer et al., 1999; Kuriyan and Cowburn, 1997; Rahuel et al., 1996).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: In the three viral proteins analyzed (A36, p14, and YL126), Grb2 binding is C-terminal to that of Nck.
source: It is curious that in the three viral proteins our lab has analyzed that are capable of promoting actin polymerisation via Nck and Grb2, namely A36, p14 and YL126 of Yaba-Like Disease Virus (Dodding and Way, 2009), Grb2 binding is C-terminal to that of Nck.
evidence: This is an observation from the authors' work supported by a citation.

claim: There is no functional evidence for Grb2-binding sites upstream of Nck in any integral membrane protein.
source: It is also striking that there is no functional evidence for Grb2-binding sites upstream of Nck in any integral membrane protein.
evidence: This is an observation based on the authors' knowledge of the literature.

claim: Grb2 is not recruited to Vaccinia in the absence of N-WASP even when its SH2-binding site on A36 is available.
source: Interestingly, Grb2 is not recruited to Vaccinia in the absence of N-WASP even when its SH2-binding site on A36 is available (Weisswange et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: In the A36 G-N virus, the SH3-PxxP binding between Grb2 and N-WASP is likely suboptimal.
source: It is likely that in the A36 G-N virus, the SH3-PxxP binding between Grb2 and N-WASP is suboptimal.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental observations.

claim: The configuration of SH2-binding pTyr motifs is critical for optimising downstream SH3 domain interactions that lead to actin polymerisation.
source: Taken together we favour that the configuration of SH2-binding pTyr motifs is critical for optimising downstream SH3 domain interactions that lead to actin polymerisation.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental observations.

claim: Specific pTyr motif configurations achieve optimal signalling output (actin polymerisation) in modular signalling involving disordered regions of proteins.
source: Our finding that specific pTyr motif configurations achieve optimal signalling output (actin polymerisation) is highly relevant to modular signalling involving disordered regions of proteins.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental observations.

claim: Disordered proteins constitute 40% of the human proteome and are rich in short linear motifs (SLiMs).
source: Disordered proteins, which constitute 40% of the human proteome, are rich in short linear motifs (SLiMs) (Tompa et al., 2014; van der Lee et al., 2014; Wright and Dyson, 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: CAR T-cell phenotypes were found to strongly depend on motif positioning in combinatorial libraries of non-natural SLiMs.
source: More recently, CAR T-cell phenotypes were found to strongly depend on motif positioning in combinatorial libraries of non-natural SLiMs (Daniels et al., 2022).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: Viral proteins are enriched in disordered regions with short host-mimicking motifs.
source: Moreover, as viral proteins are enriched in disordered regions with short host-mimicking motifs (Davey et al., 2011; Uversky, 2019), they offer unique tools to explore the importance of SLiMs positioning on signalling output.
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Vaccinia provides an excellent platform to dissect physiological or synthetic signalling networks activated by Src and Abl family kinases.
source: Our observations also demonstrate that Vaccinia provides an excellent platform to dissect physiological or synthetic signalling networks activated by Src and Abl family kinases.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental work presented.
